verses.1: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind and said:
verses.2: "Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
verses.3: Gird up your loins like a man. I will question you, and you shall answer me.
verses.4: Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth? Tell me if you have understanding.
verses.5: Who determined its measurements, since you know? Or who stretched the line upon it?
verses.6: On what were its bases sunk? Or who laid its cornerstone,
verses.7: when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
verses.8: "Who shut in the sea with doors when it burst forth from the womb,
verses.9: when I made clouds its garment and thick darkness a swaddling band for it,
verses.10: when I set limits for it and fastened a bar on its doors,
verses.11: and said, 'You may come this far and no farther; here your proud waves must stop'?
verses.12: "Have you commanded the morning since your days began, and caused the dawn to know its place,
verses.13: so that it might take hold of the ends of the earth and the wicked be shaken out of it?
verses.14: It is changed like clay under the seal, and all things appear as a garment.
verses.15: The wicked are kept from their light, and the arm that is raised is broken.
verses.16: "Have you entered into the springs of the sea or walked in the recesses of the deep?
verses.17: Have the gates of death been shown to you, or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
verses.18: Have you understood the breadth of the earth? Declare, if you know all this.
verses.19: "Where is the way to the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness,
verses.20: that you may take it to its boundary and that you may know the paths to its house?
verses.21: You know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is many!
verses.22: "Have you entered the storehouses of snow, or have you seen the storehouses of hail,
verses.23: which I have reserved for the time of distress, for the day of war and battle?
verses.24: Where is the way that the light is distributed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
verses.25: Who has carved a channel for the flood, or a path for the thunder?
verses.26: To water a land where no one dwells, a desert without a man in it,
verses.27: to satisfy the parched ground and cause the sprouting of vegetation?
verses.28: "Does rain have a father, or who fathers the drops of dew?
verses.29: From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?
verses.30: The waters become hard like stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
verses.31: "Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion?
verses.32: Can you lead forth the constellations in their seasons, or guide the Bear with her cubs?
verses.33: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish their rule over the earth?
verses.34: "Can you raise your voice to the clouds, so that an abundance of waters may cover you?
verses.35: Can you send forth lightnings, and they may say to you, 'Here we are'?
verses.36: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts, or given understanding to the mind?
verses.37: Who can number the clouds by wisdom, or pour out the bottles of heaven?
verses.38: "When the dust becomes hard and the clods stick together,
verses.39: can you hunt the prey for the lion and satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
verses.40: so they may lie down in their dens and dwell in the thicket and wait in ambush?
verses.41: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry to God and wander for lack of food?

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?" — This translation interprets the Hebrew as a rhetorical question, emphasizing the accusation that Job speaks without wisdom.
- v. 4: "Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth?" — The Hebrew uses "yasdi" for "laid the foundation," which is rendered in natural English as "laid the foundation."
- v. 29: "From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?" — The Hebrew uses poetic imagery to personify the origins of ice and frost.
- v. 40-41: "Who provides food for the raven..." — The Hebrew uses "korav" for "raven," and the passage uses poetic parallelism to highlight divine provision.

[1] Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind and said:

[2] "Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?

[3] Gird up your loins like a man. I will question you, and you shall answer me.

[4] Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth? Tell me if you have understanding.

[5] Who determined its measurements, since you know? Or who stretched the line upon it?

[6] On what were its bases sunk? Or who laid its cornerstone,

[7] when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

[8] "Who shut in the sea with doors when it burst forth from the womb,

[9] when I made clouds its garment and thick darkness a swaddling band for it,

[10] when I set limits for it and fastened a bar on its doors,

[11] and said, 'You may come this far and no farther; here your proud waves must stop'?

[12] "Have you commanded the morning since your days began, and caused the dawn to know its place,

[13] so that it might take hold of the ends of the earth and the wicked be shaken out of it?

[14] It is changed like clay under the seal, and all things appear as a garment.

[15] The wicked are kept from their light, and the arm that is raised is broken.

[16] "Have you entered into the springs of the sea or walked in the recesses of the deep?

[17] Have the gates of death been shown to you, or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?

[18] Have you understood the breadth of the earth? Declare, if you know all this.

[19] "Where is the way to the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness,

[20] that you may take it to its boundary and that you may know the paths to its house?

[21] You know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is many!

[22] "Have you entered the storehouses of snow, or have you seen the storehouses of hail,

[23] which I have reserved for the time of distress, for the day of war and battle?

[24] Where is the way that the light is distributed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?

[25] Who has carved a channel for the flood, or a path for the thunder?

[26] To water a land where no one dwells, a desert without a man in it,

[27] to satisfy the parched ground and cause the sprouting of vegetation?

[28] "Does rain have a father, or who fathers the drops of dew?

[29] From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?

[30] The waters become hard like stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

[31] "Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion?

[32] Can you lead forth the constellations in their seasons, or guide the Bear with her cubs?

[33] Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish their rule over the earth?

[34] "Can you raise your voice to the clouds, so that an abundance of waters may cover you?

[35] Can you send forth lightnings, and they may say to you, 'Here we are'?

[36] Who has put wisdom in the inward parts, or given understanding to the mind?

[37] Who can number the clouds by wisdom, or pour out the bottles of heaven?

[38] "When the dust becomes hard and the clods stick together,

[39] can you hunt the prey for the lion and satisfy the appetite of the young lions,

[40] so they may lie down in their dens and dwell in the thicket and wait in ambush?

[41] Who provides food for the raven when its young cry to God and wander for lack of food?

Notes
- v. 2: "Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?" — This translation interprets the Hebrew as a rhetorical question, emphasizing the accusation that Job speaks without wisdom.
- v. 4: "Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth?" — The Hebrew uses "yasdi" for "laid the foundation," which is rendered in natural English as "laid the foundation."
- v. 29: "From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?" — The Hebrew uses poetic imagery to personify the origins of ice and frost.
- v. 40-41: "Who provides food for the raven..." — The Hebrew uses "korav" for "raven," and the passage uses poetic parallelism to highlight divine provision.
